summary: Describes a profile of the general MPLS loss, delay, and throughput measurement techniques from RFC 6374, tailored to MPLS Transport Profile networks. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines an optional subset of MPLS measurement procedures for MPLS transport networks. It sets default settings and message intervals for loss and delay measurements.

subtitle: An optional subset of MPLS measurement procedures tailored to MPLS transport networks.

tldr.problem: The general MPLS loss and delay measurement procedures include options beyond the needs of MPLS-based transport networks.
tldr.mechanism: This profile selects a subset of RFC 6374 procedures and sets default parameters for externally configured loss and delay sessions.
tldr.outcome: Use of the profile is optional, and the RFC adds no security considerations beyond those in RFC 6374.

today: RFC 6375 is an Informational document, and the unit metadata lists no update or replacement. The measurement profile is optional.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope of the Profile
sections.content:
RFC 6374 defines procedures for measuring packet loss, delay and throughput in MPLS networks. RFC 6375 selects a simplified subset intended to meet the specific requirements of MPLS-based transport networks described in RFC 5921 and RFC 5860.

The profile is optional. Implementations may provide additional RFC 6374 functionality. It assumes that measurement devices are configured externally, for example by a Network Management System.
sections.plainLanguage: The profile picks the parts of the general measurement procedures that fit MPLS transport networks. Operators do not have to use this profile, and other RFC 6374 features remain possible.

sections.title: Measurement Considerations
sections.content: The measurement considerations in Section 2.9 of RFC 6374 also apply to MPLS-TP, except for considerations about Equal Cost Multipath and direct Loss Measurement in certain Label Switched Paths. The RFC says these exceptions concern topologies excluded from MPLS-TP.
sections.plainLanguage: Most of the measurement guidance from RFC 6374 still applies. The profile excludes two topics tied to network layouts that MPLS-TP does not use.

sections.title: Packet Loss Measurement Defaults
sections.content:
When a loss-measurement session is configured externally, both endpoints can use fixed parameter values without negotiating them. Defaults include an in-band response request, packet counting, traffic-class-scoped measurement and a truncated IEEE 1588v2 origin timestamp.

The RFC advises implementations to validate received values so configuration mismatches can be detected. Operators should be able to configure message rates per channel. Loss messages should support intervals of 100 milliseconds, 1 second, 10 seconds, 1 minute and 10 minutes. Test messages should support 10 milliseconds, 100 milliseconds, 1 second, 10 seconds and 1 minute.
sections.plainLanguage: Endpoints can agree on measurement settings through configuration rather than negotiating them in messages. Implementations should still check received settings and support the listed message intervals.

sections.title: Packet Delay Measurement and Security
sections.content:
For delay measurement, the default query requests an in-band response. The querier, responder and responder's preferred timestamp formats all default to truncated IEEE 1588v2. Implementations are strongly advised to validate received values.

Delay-measurement messages should be configurable per channel with intervals of 1 second, 10 seconds, 1 minute and 10 minutes. The RFC introduces no new security considerations; the considerations in RFC 6374 also apply.
sections.plainLanguage: Delay measurements use fixed timestamp settings by default, and received values should be checked. The security guidance comes from the general measurement specification.
